title: Woody Herman and the 'World on a String' date with Hodges and Brown
summary: With Woody Herman, Leeman recommends borrowing Ellington men while Duke's band was off, and Johnny Hodges and Lawrence Brown join the session.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And Woody Herman, whom I went to after Charlie, was the same way -- and that was 1942, '43 and '44. He was the same way, just play -- I hired you because I want you, I want your drumming, and I developed a little more -- little by little, working with great musicians, and I've got some of Duke's now in the band, some record dates, and I suggested that.
Name some.

Well, one of my great loves in life, was Ben Webster, who I ended up playing with in a quartet. Ben, yes -- and I suggested, it was during war time, and we needed men, we went out to do a record date, and ...
You needed men because it was war time? It sounds like ...
No, I put that in the wrong perspective.
I think you should rectify that, then.

Woody was listening to me talk one night coming in from New Jersey, and I said -- we were talking about the Ellington band -- and I said they're off next week, because I knew what they were doing all the time. They had been playing at that place on 49th Street, they had about 90 names.
The Zanzibar!
The Zanzibar was one, and there was something else -- Pago Pago Bay.
49th and Broadway was ...
I worked there with Pop City with Charlie Barnet after awhile, but it changed names.
But 49th and Broadway was in the Brill building
That's right. It was Bop City at one time.
Well, what about -- you said you worked with Ben Webster, which we were trying to get to. How did that come about?
Woody Herman had a couple of record dates -- one of them was "World on A String."
I didn't make that many swinging dates with Woody -- recording, but I was with him for two and a half years. We were doing mostly theatres.
Well, we're trying to get to Bill now.

When we came to New York, Duke's band was off, I mentioned to Woody, and he said, "Gees, we're doing a record date this week, I could use some people, because we were losing people to the draft -- that puts that in the proper perspective.
Yeah, right.

So he says, "Jonny Hodges, I'd love to have" -- he said -- "do you suppose he'd do that?" And I said I didn't know, that he'd have to call him. And Ben, my whole life with Ben was just starting then, you know, I was around all the time.
Did you recommend Bill? Were you the one who recommended Bill?
I recommended Ben, and he got Johnny Hodges, and when I came in for the record date, I was surprised that he got what's his name on trombone.
Lawrence Brown?
Lawrence Brown, Brownie. And they were on String and I forget what the other sides were.
"World on a String", with Woody Herman.
Yes.
